state:
**Goal `ldap`, Stage 4.** `nvs-config` reads `[ldap.<name>]` and `[capabilities.ldap]` (`crates/nvs-config/src/ldap.rs`'s module doc owns the block's rules), and `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/mod.rs` now opens connections at the Rust level: `connect` (grant by name, URL and address failover, the pool under an `ldap:` key), `open` (grant by host, then the address policy), `who_am_i`, and `Held` as the pooled `HeldConnection`. Its module doc owns those rules. Nothing is registered in `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/registry.rs` yet, so no Novis program can call `Core\Ldap`.

`crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs` holds three of the five tests `nvs-stdlib-ldap-connect-open-and-search` names, and all three pass against `samba-ad`. Still missing: `an_attribute_name_matches_without_case_and_keeps_the_servers_case` and `a_size_limit_the_server_hit_throws`, both of which need `search`.

A failure throws through `fault_of` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/mod.rs:115` as `RuntimeError`, `IOError` or `TimeoutError`, with the kind in the message. `Ldap\LdapError` does not exist yet. An `open` connection is not pooled. `rule:security/ldap-pool-is-bound-as-its-block` stays `designed` until a search left paging is shown to be closed and not pooled.

items.text: **An owned search, then `search` and `read` in `nvs_stdlib::ldap`.** `nvs_ldap::Connection::search` at `crates/nvs-ldap/src/conn.rs:381` returns a `Search<'_>` that borrows the connection, so a Novis `Ldap\Entries` cannot hold it across calls. Add a cursor the caller owns (the paging cookie and the held page) that is advanced with `&mut Connection`, and keep `is_settled` false while it pages. Then add `search` and `read` beside `who_am_i` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/mod.rs:352`: `read` is a base-scope search that returns `None` for `noSuchObject`, and a size or time limit the server hit throws (ADR 0278 § 5). Add the last two tests to `crates/nvs-stdlib/tests/ldap.rs:203`, and extend the pool test so a connection released mid-search is closed, not pooled.

**`Ldap\LdapError` with `$kind` and `$code`.** Add it to the tree at `crates/nvs-hir/src/errors.rs:115` and `OWN_PROPERTIES`, then to `ThrownClass` at `crates/nvs-runtime/src/throwable.rs:370`, and give it the `nvs_types::error_lib` property arm `Core\Db\DbError` has. Then make `fault_of` at `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/mod.rs:115` throw it. ADR 0278 § 10.

**The registry rows and helpers**: `Core\Ldap::connect`/`open`, `Ldap\Connection::search`/`read`/`whoami`, `Ldap\Entries`, `Ldap\Entry` (`dn`, `has`, `string`, `strings`, `bytes`, `toArray`), `Ldap\Settings`, `Ldap\Tls`, `Ldap\Scope`, `Ldap\ErrorKind`, with a reference card for each. Follow the way `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/db/registry.rs:228` declares `Core\Db::connect`. `search` takes a `Filter`, so this slice needs the smallest `Ldap\Filter` (`equals`, `present`) from Stage 5. Then write the two conformance cases.

backlog: `open` connections are not pooled. ADR 0278 § 4 keys that pool on every URL, the user, a password digest, the TLS mode and the CA file (`crates/nvs-stdlib/src/ldap/mod.rs` module doc).

The `ldap:` pool and memo prefix shares its namespace with a `[db."ldap:x"]` block name. The downcast to `Held` keeps the two types apart, but a memo hit would throw "closed". Not checked whether any config rule forbids that name.
